Apex Mission Systems LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume I — Technical 1. Cloud Migration Methodology Apex will migrate the 140 mission applications in the Air Force cloud environment through our Migration Factory, a repeatable pipeline that discovers, assesses, refactors and cuts over each application in waves of 12 to 15 applications. The factory begins with automated discovery: dependency mapping agents run for 14 days against each application enclave and produce a migration blueprint covering data flows, ports, identities and integration points. Blueprints are peer reviewed by the Government product owner before a wave is scheduled. On our current Air Force Materiel Command migration task order, the factory has moved 61 applications with a measured mean migration time of 4 days per application from cutover rehearsal to production, and zero unplanned Sev-1 outages in the last 9 months. Each wave ends with a hypercare period of 10 business days in which the original application team and Apex site reliability engineers share an on-call rotation.

2. Cybersecurity and Continuous ATO Apex designs every migrated application to inherit controls from the Air Force cloud platform authorization and documents the remaining application-level controls in eMASS before cutover. After initial authorization, Apex maintains a continuous ATO. Automated control evidence collectors run daily, push results to eMASS, and open findings in the program's risk register within 24 hours of detection. The authorizing official receives a monthly control health summary. Container images are rebuilt weekly from hardened Iron Bank bases, scanned in the pipeline, and blocked from promotion on any critical vulnerability.

3. Legacy Application Rationalization Before migration, Apex scores every application on mission value, technical health and cost to run using the TIME model (tolerate, invest, migrate, eliminate). The rationalization board, chaired by the Government, decides the disposition of each application. On comparable programs this step retired or consolidated 18 to 22 percent of the portfolio before migration, avoiding the cost of moving applications with no remaining mission owner.

Helix Research Technology LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation 75N910-27-R-0044 — Research Data Platform and Analytics Support Department of Health and Human Services — National Institutes of Health Volume I — Technical 1. Data Platform Architecture Helix proposes a FedRAMP High research data platform built on a lakehouse architecture with separate zones for raw, curated and analysis-ready data, and with compute that scales to zero between analyses to control cost. All datasets are registered in a searchable catalog with lineage from source instrument or study to every derived table.

2. Privacy and Controlled-Access Data Protection Controlled-access human-subjects data is held in a separate enclave. Access follows a dbGaP-aligned workflow: a researcher requests a dataset, the data access committee approves the request, and the platform issues time-bound, purpose-limited access that expires automatically. No controlled-access data can be exported from the enclave; results leave only after automated disclosure review and, where required, a human privacy officer check.
3. Researcher Self-Service Analytics Researchers use managed notebooks and a no-code cohort builder against analysis-ready data, with shared, versioned environments so analyses are reproducible.

Keystone Ridge Analytics LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation W52P1J-27-R-0023 — Army Logistics Data Analytics Platform Department of the Army Volume I — Technical 1. Predictive Maintenance Analytics Keystone will deliver predictive maintenance models for ground vehicles and generators that forecast component failures 30 to 90 days ahead. The models were trained and validated on three years of Army ground-fleet maintenance history, and in a 2025 pilot with an Army sustainment brigade they cut unscheduled maintenance by 18 percent. Every model publishes its accuracy, drift and the data it was trained on to a model registry, so maintainers can see why a part was flagged before acting on it.

2. Data Integration with GCSS-Army The platform exchanges data with GCSS-Army in both directions through the Army's approved interface, and this integration is already authorized under an Army RMF package from our current task order. Legacy STAMIS feeds are mapped into the same data model during transition. Units that operate disconnected keep a local analytics node that synchronizes when the network returns, so forecasts remain available in the field.

3. Cybersecurity and RMF Keystone will inherit controls from the Army cloud environment and implement the remaining controls before the platform carries production data, with continuous monitoring evidence fed to eMASS.

Harborview Student Systems Inc Proposal in response to RFP WUSD-RFP-27-014 — Student Information System Willowmere Unified School District Section 1 — Functional and Technical Response 1. State Reporting, Enrollment and Attendance Harborview's state reporting is Ed-Fi certified and exchanges enrollment, attendance, discipline, course and staff data with the State's Ed-Fi ODS/API nightly. Automated validation checks every record against the state's business rules before submission, so errors are corrected at the school before a deadline rather than after. At our reference districts every state submission over the last three years was accepted on first filing. Attendance is taken by period or by day from the teacher's class list on any device. Unexcused absences trigger parent notifications within 15 minutes, and chronic absence dashboards flag students who have missed 10 percent or more of enrolled days.

2. Scheduling, Gradebook and Special Education The master scheduler builds secondary schedules from course requests, balances sections and resolves conflicts automatically, and counselors can run what-if scenarios before publishing. The gradebook supports standards-based and traditional grading and posts report cards and transcripts directly from teacher grades. Special education, IEP and Section 504 management are built into the core product, not a separate add-on. Case managers draft IEPs, schedule meetings, track service minutes and progress monitoring, and produce state special education child count reports from the same student record.

3. Parent and Student Portal, Security and Privacy Families use a single portal and mobile app, available in 14 languages, to view grades, attendance, schedules and fees and to complete annual registration online. Students see assignments and grades with the same sign-in, and the District's SSO/SAML identity provider is supported for staff and students. Student data is encrypted in transit and at rest, access is role-based down to the field level, and every change to a student record is logged.
